data.name: App_Tagline
data.value: Return your session to its fresh-start state — without rebooting.

data.name: Main_Memory_Tooltip
data.value: Memory details and the optional Deep Memory Cleanup

data.name: Main_BaselineHintNone
data.value: Make the current state the baseline

data.name: Banner_NoBaseline
data.value: No baseline yet. When your computer is in the state you consider clean (for example shortly after starting Windows), click “Make current state the baseline”.

data.name: Banner_PreviousBoot
data.value: The baseline was created before the last restart, so apps are matched by name and location only. Consider creating a fresh baseline.

data.name: Banner_Elevated
data.value: SnapBack is running as administrator. This is not needed, and apps that run as administrator are never closed. If User Account Control is turned off, all your apps run elevated and SnapBack shows them as protected.

data.name: Main_MakeBaseline_Tooltip
data.value: Everything running right now becomes the clean state SnapBack returns to.

data.name: Tab_Kept_Description
data.value: Apps that were part of the baseline (or are in your keep list). SnapBack never suggests closing them; new windows or child processes they open are fine.

data.name: Tab_Protected_Description
data.value: Windows components, services, elevated programs and anything SnapBack cannot fully verify. These are never closed, no matter what is selected.

data.name: Main_NothingNew
data.value: Nothing new since the baseline. Your session is already in its clean state.

data.name: Sort_Tooltip
data.value: Sort by this column (click again to reverse)

data.name: Main_AlwaysKeep_Tooltip
data.value: Never suggest these apps again (your keep list)

data.name: Memory_StandbyHint
data.value: cache that Windows hands to apps instantly; counts as available

data.name: Memory_ModifiedHint
data.value: changed data waiting to be written to disk; never cleared by SnapBack

data.name: Memory_DeepWhat
data.value: Clears the standby cache: data Windows keeps in memory in case it is needed again. The pages become free memory immediately.

data.name: Memory_DeepNot
data.value: It does not touch memory that apps are using (no working-set trimming), does not touch data waiting to be written to disk (modified pages), and does not change any setting.

data.name: Memory_DeepCost
data.value: Available memory barely changes, because this cache already counts as available. Windows rebuilds the cache as you work, so apps and files may open a little slower for a while. Usually you do not need this.

data.name: Memory_ModeStandbyHint
data.value: Drops all cached data that is not in use.

data.name: Memory_ModeLowHint
data.value: Drops only the least valuable cache; gentler, frees less.

data.name: Memory_UacNote
data.value: Windows will ask for administrator permission for this one operation. SnapBack itself keeps running without administrator rights.

data.name: Memory_AlreadyElevated
data.value: SnapBack is running as administrator, so no permission prompt will appear.

data.name: Memory_Confirm_Text
data.value:
Clear: {0}.
No app is closed and no data is lost; Windows will rebuild the cache over time. Available memory will barely change, because this cache already counts as available.
Continue?

data.name: Memory_ResultExplain
data.value: The reclaimed cache moved to free memory. It was already counted as available, so “Available” changes little — that is expected.

data.name: Settings_LanguageHint
data.value: The language changes immediately. Unsupported system languages fall back to English.

data.name: Settings_Timeout
data.value: Seconds to wait for each app to close (5–120)

data.name: Settings_PreselectCaution
data.value: Also pre-select apps marked with a caution (possible unsaved data, browsers, …)

data.name: Settings_ClosingHint
data.value: Apps that need manual review (scripts, consoles, background processes) are never pre-selected, and nothing is ever force-terminated without asking.

data.name: Settings_AutoBaselineEnable
data.value: Create a baseline automatically after I sign in to Windows

data.name: Settings_AutoBaselineHint
data.value: SnapBack starts briefly at sign-in, waits until startup apps have finished launching, saves the baseline and exits. It adds one entry to your Startup apps; nothing else is changed.

data.name: Settings_MinDelay
data.value: Wait at least this many seconds after sign-in

data.name: Settings_Quiet
data.value: …and until no new apps have started for this many seconds

data.name: Settings_KeepListHint
data.value: These apps are treated as part of your clean state and are never suggested for closing. Add apps with “Always keep selected” in the main window.
